rh.number_traceability.prose_claims_cons.reason: The numbers in the prose are macros generated from the logs, but several prose claims built on them are contradicted by those same logs. (a) The Analysis says 'the best model in this entire study is an isotropic compressive scaling of an additive metric on CIE LCh coordinates', which is M1-hcl at chromatic chord held-out LL -1.822. The paper's own appendix table, which it calls 'all four primary configurations', lists models with higher held-out LL on the same chromatic held-out ratings and folds. In arc coordinates: M3-opponent -1.722, M3-hcl -1.756, M2 -1.781. In the joint chord fit: M3-hcl -1.795. In the joint arc fit: M3-opponent -1.686 and M3-ciergb -1.764. The arc half of the same isotropy diagnostic, which the paper only points to by filename, shows the best model there is the per-axis opponent model, and CIELAB's isotropic metric is significantly worse than the cone one (-0.081 [-0.166,-0.001]). The paper calls this claim 'a stronger and cleaner statement of the null'. (b) The paper says the observed M2-best M3 value (-0.1126) lies 'inside the non-cone ones' (the synthetic reference intervals). It falls just outside two of the five: the opponent-generated interval [-0.1119,-0.0058] and the CIELAB-generated interval [-0.2776,-0.1153]. (c) For the coarse two-channel models the paper says the observed values fall 'inside the non-cone one'. The observed coarse-cone minus M1 delta (+0.079) is outside the interval generated under the coarse CIELAB model [-0.106,+0.019]. (d) The failure analysis says 'f_L versus f_M. Unidentifiable by construction on this stimulus set'. This contradicts the logged synthetic recovery (L-M contrast recovered at 0.198 [0.139,0.249] against a true 0.196, correct sign in 100% of runs) and the paper's own verdict that 'the resolvable granularity is the three-cone split'. None of this is fabrication. However, (a) and (d) are categorical claims about results that their underlying sources materially contradict.

rh.code_paper_alignment.methodology_matc.reason: The Methodology matches the code on everything substantive: the model family and outer Box-Cox form; monotone PCHIP inner functions with knots at training-fold quantiles; unit-RMS axis scaling and per-dataset design scaling computed from training data; the gauge reference r_k=1; per-dataset observation models (Thurstonian with per-observer scale for Wiebel and a single scale for gray; Gaussian with profiled per-subject gain and SD for Helm and Ekman); 5-fold x 10-repeat folds disjoint by evaluation unit; the paired cluster bootstrap with argmax inside each resample; the arc and chord coordinates; and the gray pipeline. There are some inaccuracies of detail. (i) The paper twice says the power analysis 'ran the identical CV comparison'. The code uses repeats=1 and n_restarts=6, against 10 and 10 for the real run. The log's own note says 'identical CV protocol' while its config fields show the reduced settings. (ii) The Wiebel CV is called 'pair-disjoint' but is disjoint by triad. (iii) 'Every model comparison is run twice', yet the robustness variants are chord-only. (iv) '10 restarts per fit' holds for the main CV but not for the auxiliary fits. The models, fold type, metric and selection rule in the power analysis are the same as in the real run. Its reduced repeats widen the synthetic reference distributions, which makes the main power inferences conservative rather than inflated. I therefore judge these to fall short of a material contradiction.

rh.identifiability_disclosure.no_overcla.reason: The paper does not claim established cone specificity. Its verdict is negative, and it explicitly declines to adjudicate the mechanism question. The earned-null claim is consistent with the logged held-out, power and recovery results. The selection-aware M2-best M3 delta is negative in all 16 logged specifications, and its CI excludes zero in the joint fits. Under a generator built from the fitted cone parameters, the delta is +0.040 [-0.012,+0.086] and M2 wins the panel 91% of the time; the observed -0.113 lies below that range. Under the nearest (opponent) control generator, the correct basis wins 94% of the time. Recovery of distinct f_L, f_M, f_S succeeds, with median errors of 2-3% of range. The paper also states that its pair-resampling bootstrap CI ([-0.355,+0.007]) reaches the lower edge of the cone-generated range, and that the observed anisotropy matches what the fitted cone model would produce. The marginal 'inside the non-cone ones' misstatement and the stale 'unidentifiable' failure-analysis sentence are assessed under prose consistency. They do not turn the earned-null claim into a contradiction of the results.

Only provided data are used (data/gray, data/chromatic, data/cone_fundamentals). The cone conversion uses the provided CIE 2006 fundamentals, with stated reference whites (D65/C/E) and von Kries normalization verified to (1,1,1). integrity.execution_claims.reason: The paper delegates deviation disclosure to attempts_log.md. That file's section A is headed '(all disclosed in the paper)'. Its item A.3 states: 'Bounds were widened to [-8, 3] before any reported run. In the reported runs the bound is inactive for M1 and M2; it is occasionally active at rho = 3 for the CIELAB/LCh controls in the joint configuration, which is logged in fitlog_*.csv and noted as a limitation.' The logged fits establish this inspection claim is false. M1's rho sits at the lower bound -8 in all 50 folds of the reported 'no per-dataset design scaling' specification. M2's rho hits a bound in 14 of the 16 reported configurations: 5/50 folds at -8 in the primary chromatic chord run, and 26/50 at +3 in joint arc. The bound activity among controls is understated: M3-opponent, the best control in joint arc, is at +3 in 46/50 folds; M3-cielab, the best control in the primary run, is at -8 in 13/50; M3-hcl is at +3 in 38/50 folds of joint chord. report.tex never mentions the rho bounds or their activity, so 'noted as a limitation' and 'all disclosed in the paper' are also false. These are explicit claims about the executed fits and about a disclosure, and the artifacts contradict them, not merely fail to support them. Two smaller procedural overstatements point the same way: 'ran the identical CV comparison' for the power runs (1 repeat and 6 restarts in practice), and 'none [of the paper's numbers] is typed by hand' (some descriptive values, such as d(434,674)=0.84 and hue angles of 90.8 and 84.4 degrees, are typed in).
